# Cedric Stanhope

## Overview

- **Age:** sixteen  <sub>[v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c8 P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052)</sub>
- **Origin:** Boston, United States  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- **Role:** poet and student  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033), [v4 c17 P27](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0027)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Yankee  <sub>[v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>

## Appearance

In his childhood, Cedric was unusually small for his years, possessing a delicate, refined face, extremely dark blue eyes, and chestnut curls. As he grew older, he cut his curls short into brown hair and eventually grew into an impressive six-foot-tall young man.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)_

## Personality

Cedric is an extraordinarily imaginative, intelligent, and meditative individual who maintains a poetic worldview. He is gentlemanly, bashful, cleanly, and possesses a strong sense of manliness, fairness, and deep loyalty to those he loves. As he grew older, his youthful fancy for fairies evolved into an active interest in sports like football alongside his writing.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021), [v2 c7 P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), [v2 c8 P32](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0032), [v2 c8 P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c23 P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), [v2 c28 P10](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0010), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)_

## History

Cedric moved from the United States to Brierley to live with his grandmother near the shore road, attending the local school under teacher Nell Harcourt. He quickly formed a deep bond with Nell as a kindred spirit. Through a letter to his father, Stephen Stanhope, Cedric unintentionally reunited Stephen with his former love, Rosalind Penrose, whom Cedric accepted as a beloved mother figure. Over the years, he grew significantly in height and pursued his passion for creative writing, having several of his poems published in magazines. He made a point to attend Nell's wedding, where he drove the bride and groom to the train station and wrote a praised poem inspired by the ceremony. Later at age sixteen, he made plans to travel abroad for two years of study.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c29 P5](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0005), [v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004), [v4 c3 P5](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0005), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033), [v4 c4 P16](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0016), [v4 c17 P27](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0027)_

## Quotes

> I ask you to take these, teacher, which I discovered in the field belonging to Mr. Duckett, and I returned so I could offer them to you since I believed you were a lady who would appreciate them, and also because . . . teacher, I am fond of you.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> I didn’t become really acquainted with him until my little mother had died. However, once you do come to know him, he is splendid. I love him most of all in the world, and then Grandma Stanhope, and after that, you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009)</sub>

> Is it not wonderful that we are that type, teacher?  <sub>[v2 c15 P19](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0019)</sub>

> Because, as you understand, teacher, that title is reserved exclusively for my own dear mother, so I am unable to use it for anybody else. Instead, I address her as ‘Mother Rosalind’ and she is second in my affection only to father.  <sub>[v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>

> After you get married, calling you Mrs. Carrow is something I WILL NOT do. For me, your name will forever be 'Teacher’—the instructor who gave me the finest lessons I was ever taught.  <sub>[v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>
